Any notebook can open a GridflowClient. The gridflow_models notebook module wraps one and returns pandas: setup_notebook() hands back data, models and common.
Every stage is one command that is safe to re-run and records its own run, so it runs under any orchestrator, such as cron, Airflow or Dagster, as a task.
Sources above ground; bronze, silver and gold below; the readers at the foot. Each part is keyed to its file on GitHub. The chartreuse cable is the route of the row followed below.

Section drawing of gridflow. Above ground, the vendor sources stand as the assets they report on: Elexon at a substation, NESO carbon intensity at a gas-fired power station, the NESO Data Portal at a solar farm and Open-Meteo at a met mast on the British side; ENTSO-E at a converter station, ENTSO-G at a gas entry point, GIE AGSI at storage tanks and GIE ALSI at an LNG terminal across the sea. A cable runs down from each through its own connector into bronze, where each response is kept as a file with a sidecar; transformers carry each on into silver Parquet. Plain views gather every silver dataset into one DuckDB file that straddles silver and gold; the Elexon cable also runs on to the gold builder. At the foot, the gridflow command and GridflowClient read that file; notebooks read through the client, which the gridflow_models notebook module wraps to return pandas; and gridflow_models training and backtests read silver Parquet directly as of a time.

A notebook reads it into pandas

The gridflow_models notebook module wraps a GridflowClient and returns pandas at the notebook boundary. query reads the _latest view, so period 37 comes back once, as 110.0. Timestamps arrive in local time; the snippet converts published_at, Elexon's publication time, to UTC.
